newsitem.title: USA: Accord reached on Kelly Air Force base transfer.
newsitem.headline: Accord reached on Kelly Air Force base transfer.

text.p: In a landmark pact, San Antonio, Texas, and the U.S. Air Force Thursday agreed on terms under which the City would take control of Kelly Air Force Base.

"The arrangement that has been worked out is the first of its kind," Teresa Nino, manager of public affairs and community relations for the Greater Kelly Development Corp, a community group the city council ordained in late 1995 to help ease the economic sting from the base's closure.
"The way it works out is that we will not have to pay on it unless we are making a profit from the commercialization going on here," Nino said.

The base's value has been estimated at $108 million, she said. Once the base properties begin throwing off revenues, the city will have 22 years to pay off the cost using rents from private contractors.

"In any new business venture, it takes a couple of years before it actually can start seeng some profits," Nino said. "This way it doesn't hurt the community by trying to make payments on something when it's not making money."
Nino said while the use of bonds has been brought up from time to time as a means of funding the transfer, no formal discussions have taken place.
In addition to signing the transfer terms document, known as the economic development conveyance, San Antonio and the Air Force signed two other transfer-related documents, she said.
The the pair signed a promissory note documents, which are essentially mortgage documents relating to the purchase. They define the principal, interest and payment terms.

A third document, referred to as the "lease and furtherance of conveyance" or "master lease," outlines terms under which San Antonio would gradually utilize buildings as the Air Force scales back. The Air Force will not completely vacate the base until 2001.

"Once the Air Force completes its commitment for environmental clean up and other things it's committed to, then the lease is then (turned) into a transfer of deeds," Nino said. "And that's the actual real estate transfer."
The Greater Kelly Development Corp was the legacy of 167 community leaders who banded together after the Air Force announced the base's shut down in 1995, she said.
